snippet.title: She Turned An Ancestral Home Into Bangalore's Most Interesting Address | Tikki Talk Ep 14
snippet.description:
What does it take to turn a 1949 ancestral home into Bangalore's most beloved cultural address?

Rohit Kapoor spends a day at The Courtyard with Akhila Srinivas, architect, cultural curator, and the quiet force behind one of the city's most interesting spaces. From a government auction in 1949 to a wine bar, an audiophile listening room, and a conservatory that has hosted 55+ of India's best chefs The Courtyard is unlike anything else in Bangalore.

Also featuring Kavan, the chef behind Naru, one of the hardest tables to get in the city.

A conversation about food, culture, community, and what it means to build something that refuses to become irrelevant.

snippet.title: Architecture, Coffee & Poi-challenge | The Second House, Goa | Tikki Talk Ep.12 Ft Dishant Pritamani
snippet.description:
In this episode of Tikki Talk, I sit down with Dishant Pritamani at Second House, Goa, a space that feels less like a restaurant and more like someone’s second home.

Set inside an old Indo-Portuguese bungalow, Second House was designed to feel lived-in, not showroom-ready. From mapping imperfections using AI to weaving local craft into the space, every detail is intentional  but never loud.
We speak about what changes when a founder evolves.

When growth stops being about scale and starts becoming about expression.

About building slower, caring more about craft, and choosing depth over noise.

We also talk about Cafe Lento, the philosophy of slowing down, and why sometimes the boldest move in business is restraint.
And somewhere between architecture and espresso, we ended up blindfolded… stacking poi.

If you're interested in entrepreneurship, hospitality, design thinking, or simply conversations that don’t rush, this one’s for you.

snippet.title: The Café Delhi Heights Story: From Juicy Lucy to a Modern Icon | Tikki Talk Ep. 11 Ft. Vikrant Batra
snippet.description:
Some places serve food.
Others serve memory.

The iconic Juicy Lucy Burger is one of those dishes that keeps you coming back. And for me, @cafedelhiheights7214  has been that place for over a decade where the food, the people, and the warmth start to feel like home.

In this episode of Tikki Talk, Rohit Kapoor sits down with Vikrant Batra, the force behind Café Delhi Heights since 2011. From building a neighbourhood favourite into a beloved brand, to blending tradition with a distinctly cosmopolitan energy, this is a story of steady passion and thoughtful growth.

And now, the next generation is writing its own chapter. With Sarthak leading Ikigai by CDH, fresh ideas meet familiar warmth pet-friendly, contemporary, yet rooted.

A full-circle conversation about food, family, and building something that lasts.

Watch now and you’ll understand why some tables are worth returning to.
